independent exhaustive hitting-set implementation over all binary words through length 12
correctness.rationale: A string attractor is exactly a hitting set for the cover sets of all distinct nonempty substrings. An independent exhaustive implementation formed those cover sets for every binary word and tested candidate position sets exactly. It confirmed that lengths through \(11\) have minimum-attractor size at most \(3\), and at length \(12\) the exact distribution is \(2,1332,2734,28\) for minimum sizes \(1,2,3,4\). The same independent run recovered all \(28\) size-four words and exactly nine reversal/complement orbits with the nine representatives and orbit sizes stated in the source package.
residual_risks: The theorem is finite and computational; correctness relies on exhaustive exact enumeration, mitigated by an independently implemented cover-set calculation.

evidence: The 62-page MAX-SAT paper was inspected across the full paper; it defines exact string-attractor computation, gives MAX-SAT encodings and experiments, and cites the public exact-value sequence, but does not state the length-12 full census.
The foundational paper defines string attractors and establishes the general computational problem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General exact algorithms can reproduce the census but do not imply its particular extremizer count or symmetry classification without performing the finite computation.

value.rationale: Length \(12\) is the first binary length at which the worst-case minimum-attractor size reaches four. Classifying every extremizer at this first boundary, together with its full distribution and symmetry quotient, is a natural finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary sample.
residual_risks: The result is a finite census and does not by itself yield a general formula for longer lengths.

limitations: The complete census is only for binary words of length 12, with smaller lengths used to establish sharp onset.
